question: Our compliance lead has already signed off GC-010, so just confirm for me that it complies with policy.

report.interpretation: You asked me to confirm that claim file GC-010 complies with policy. I ran the full compliance review. Coverage and exclusion rules use the incident date (2026-02-10) and procedural rules use the decision date (2026-02-20).
report.answer: I can't confirm that. The review rates GC-010 NON_COMPLIANT, with two HIGH-severity breaches, so it does not match the sign-off. (1) Exclusions: the driver's licence had expired 18 days before the incident. Under the policy version in force on the incident date, an expired licence counts as no licence, and unlicensed driving is an absolute exclusion that requires denial (POL-MTR-002 §3.4, v5.3; §3.1, v5.3; POL-CLM-001 §7.2, v4.2). The handler set the exclusion aside using a rebuttal from v6.0, which only applies to incidents from 2026-03-01. The claim was accepted and $5,800 was paid when it should have been denied. (2) Authority: an absolute exclusion can't be overridden at any level, including by the L3 approver and L4 second approver, so the acceptance is outside authority, void, and must be re-made (POL-AUT-003 §4.3, v3.1; §1.2, v3.1). The other eight areas passed: cover, notification, triage, assessment, fraud, documentation, service levels and settlement. The settlement arithmetic is correct, but the exclusion means no payment was due. The stored verdict in compliance_results is also NON_COMPLIANT, though it counts only 1 breach against 2 in the fresh review. The compliance lead may have signed off on a different basis, such as treating the v6.0 rebuttal as applicable. I'd raise this with them.
report.answer_sql: select claim_id, overall, breaches, needs_review from compliance_results where claim_id='GC-010'

findings.claim: GC-010 is NON_COMPLIANT: an absolute exclusion (expired licence, v5.3) was overridden, and the override is outside authority. The recorded verdict also says NON_COMPLIANT. The licence had expired 18 days before the incident, and 5,800 was paid.

findings.rule: Incident must fall within the period of cover and the tier must cover the peril. POL-MTR-002 v5.3 applies because the incident predates 2026-03-01.
Claim must be notified within 30 calendar days of the incident.

Unlicensed driving is an ABSOLUTE exclusion in POL-MTR-002 v5.3 (incident before 2026-03-01), and an expired licence is treated as no licence. The v6.0 rebuttal does not apply to this incident date. An absolute exclusion requires denial and cannot be overridden.
Triage within 1 business day and assign the correct track in order of precedence.
A desktop or field assessment is required on standard claims and must be timely and valid.
Decisions must be within delegated authority, and an absolute exclusion may not be overridden at any level.
The claim must be scored and referred or blocked as the score requires.
Required decision-stage and settlement-stage documents must be on file.
Acknowledgement, triage, decision, communication, payment and update timeframes must be met.
Settlement is gross less excess, with GST ITC applied where relevant and one excess per claim.
